correctness.rationale: For finite strictly decreasing affine maps the max/min Bellman envelopes reverse extremal roles; their two-step compositions are increasing, giving monotone parity subsequences. Each pairwise affine comparison therefore eventually stabilizes, including ties. Exact extremizer-set products imply two-step nondecreasing multiplicities, so unique winners stop or have an eventually constant optimal two-letter suffix on each parity. A no-return upper/lower-envelope argument establishes disjoint letter runs in parity subsequences. Counting ordered runs yields the stated valid O_q(n^(2q-2)) upper bound. Fraction-based tests evaluated 619210 words for 190 models and a genuine ternary example; computation is corroborative only.

This is best-knowledge originality, not certification of historical priority.

value.rationale: Motivated by recent finite-alphabet probabilistic automatic-complexity advances and a published binary regularity theorem. Obtains an exact finite-union-of-ultimately-periodic-ray characterization for fixed orientation-reversing two-state models over arbitrarily many letters, plus a uniform parity-run structural restriction and polynomial sparsity envelope. These are non-routine infinite-family structural facts, not merely rephrasings of the known binary or opposite-determinant cases.
